result.title: Guiding AI Agents to Generate Conjectures by Encoding How Theorems Build on One Another
result.summary: Recently, LLMs have been making headlines, and headway, in mathematical research. Much of this work focuses on proving existing open conjectures. Deciding what to prove is harder and less studied, because of the lack of a clear criterion for what makes a conjecture worth pursuing. We present a method for conjecture generation that builds on the observation that mathematical theorems build on one another: new theorems can modify the setting or hypotheses of earlier theorems, strengthen their conclusions, or extend their scope. We encode these relationships in a new kind of graph, the Theorem Evolution Graph (TEG), which we instantiate as an online search method for LLM agents. An agent builds a TEG in two steps: (1) identifying relevant theorems from papers found by following citations backward and forward from a seed paper; and (2) comparing those theorems to record how one builds on another. LLM judges and an expert mathematician preferred TEG-generated conjectures over those from an unconstrained baseline. LLM judges favored TEG conjectures for significance, ambition, and insight, and favored baseline conjectures for plausibility. Ablations suggest a benefit from constructing and using a TEG even when the available papers are fixed.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「定理演化图」（TEG），把定理之间修改设定、加强结论、扩展范围等承接关系显式编码为图结构，并实现为 LLM agent 的在线搜索方法，用于生成值得研究的数学猜想；LLM 评判与专家更偏好该方法生成的猜想。
AI.relevance_reason: 非视觉工作，但其用外部图结构记录实体间「如何承接」的关系并据此控制搜索与扩展，可能为 LVR 中关系型内部状态的表示及探索、停止决策提供可核查的方法线索。
